text:
Maya Chen: Hey team, just got an escalation from Acme Integrations — they report that streaming completions over EventSource in Safari are dropping after 20-30s and they see only partial outputs. They say Chrome works fine.

Customer: Acme Integrations: repro steps: 1) open our webapp (Safari 16.4 macOS) 2) call /v1/streams with EventSource to our proxy 3) stream starts then sends first chunk then closes with no error. Reconnecting sometimes yields the rest, sometimes not.

Maya Chen: They pasted the browser console log: 

```
EventSource failed to connect
EventSource connection closed (code 0)
Received partial message: \"{\"id\": \"...\", \"text\": \"Hello wo\"
```

Maya Chen: They also mentioned they host the proxy behind Cloudflare + CloudFront (CDN) and use an S3 origin for static assets.

Omar Reyes: Classic CDN + SSE friction. Two quick things to check: 1) content-type and cache headers from the SSE endpoint, 2) whether Cloudflare/CF workers or CloudFront are buffering/chunking.

Benji Patel: Pinged them for response headers — they replied with this trace from curl -v: 

```
> GET /v1/streams?id=abc HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< cache-control: max-age=0, public
< content-encoding: gzip
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< connection: keep-alive
```

Benji Patel: Aha: cache-control: max-age=0, public and content-encoding: gzip. Those are red flags for SSE. Also some CDNs will buffer responses when they see content-encoding or cacheable headers.

Maya Chen: Customer says they never set gzip on that endpoint but CloudFront injects gzip at edge.

Omar Reyes: CloudFront can do compression, and some CloudFront/Cloudflare combinations will buffer until they finish gzipping — that breaks streaming. Also Safari is more sensitive: EventSource won't see partial chunks if the server closes the connection unexpectedly or if the bytes are buffered.

SRE Bot: Suggested checks: ensure SSE responses have 
- Content-Type: text/event-stream
- Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, no-store, must-revalidate (or at least no-cache)
- Connection: keep-alive
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length)
- Avoid Content-Encoding at edge (disable gzip for SSE paths)

Maya Chen: I gave the customer a list of immediate repro steps to confirm: 
1) curl -N to ensure streaming is unbuffered: 
```
curl -v -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?id=abc
```
Look for incremental event: lines starting with "data:" arriving in chunks.

Customer: Ran that and said curl -N shows continuous events, but when hitting through their CDN URL it shows a delay and then a big chunk.

Benji Patel: That confirms edge buffering. Ask them to disable compression and any response buffering for that path. Also check Cloudflare 'Server Side Exclude' or 'Argo' features and CloudFront behavior when combining with Lambda@Edge.

Omar Reyes: Another Safari-specific thing: Safari may silently close EventSource on redirects (302/307). Do we return any redirects for auth? If users are hitting an auth gate (e.g., returning 302 to /login or 204 keepalive) that can break the EventSource handshake.

Maya Chen: Customer says they use a signed cookie for S3 and we do a short 307 for token refresh on the proxy. That could explain intermittent closes.

Customer: Is there a recommended header list for Redwood SSE endpoints?

Maya Chen: For reference we recommend (and our hosted endpoints use): 
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, must-revalidate
Pragma: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive
X-Accel-Buffering: no  # nginx
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.acme.example
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```
and ensure CDN does not gzip or buffer.

Omar Reyes: Also mention CORS preflight: EventSource does not use preflight for simple GETs, but Access-Control-Allow-Origin and optionally Allow-Credentials must match. Safari is stricter about credentials — if request includes cookies, server must set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and Access-Control-Allow-Origin cannot be '*'.

Benji Patel: Customer uses cookies for session. They had Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on the edge. That's invalid with credentials, Safari rejects it.

SRE Bot: Recommended tests: 
- Reproduce with a minimal HTML page using EventSource against origin URL (bypass CDN) and against CDN URL. 
- Add a non-cookie test (no credentials) to see if CORS/credentials are the root cause. 
- Try Safari private browsing — it sometimes enforces different caching.

Maya Chen: Customer ran quick tests: EventSource to origin (bypass CDN) works consistently in Safari. EventSource via CDN fails. When they temporarily disabled Cloudflare, Safari worked.

Omar Reyes: So root cause: CDN is transforming/ buffering the SSE stream (gzip or caching) and also the edge was setting Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Because Safari is using cookies, that combination causes early termination or refused connections.

Benji Patel: Workarounds we suggested to the customer: 
- Disable compression for SSE endpoints (on CloudFront set Compress=false for path pattern).
- Add header Cache-Control: no-transform, no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no / proxy buffering off.
- Ensure Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true and Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to the requester origin, not '*'.
- Avoid issuing 3xx redirects during the SSE connection lifecycle; perform auth before opening the stream or use token in query param/header.
- As fallback, implement a fetch() + ReadableStream polyfill for browsers where EventSource misbehaves (we provided a small polyfill snippet).

Maya Chen: Shared a polyfill example the engineering team can use (client-side fetch streaming fallback): 
```
// minimal fetch streaming fallback
async function fetchStream(url, onChunk) {
  const r = await fetch(url, { credentials: 'include' });
  const reader = r.body.getReader();
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
  let buf = '';
  while (true) {
    const { value, done } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
    let parts = buf.split('\n\n');
    buf = parts.pop();
    for (const p of parts) onChunk(p);
  }
}
```

Maya Chen: Customer asked if Redwood has any documented Safari bugs. I referenced a known Safari bug around EventSource and service worker interactions (SW intercepting and returning opaque responses) and redirect handling.

Omar Reyes: Internal notes to escalate if customer can't disable CDN: 
1) Ask CDN provider rep to mark SSE path as "origin-streaming" or "origin-passthrough". Cloudflare: disable HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 downgrades? Also set 'origin' server push settings off.
2) If they must use CDN, advise using WebSockets (which many CDNs support better) or our SDK streaming over websockets as a fallback.
3) If the proxy injects auth redirects, change flow to prefetch token and set Authorization header before opening EventSource.

Benji Patel: Also flagged a billing/usage check: repeated reconnects may create extra billable requests. We suggested rate-limiting reconnects client-side and adding jitter/backoff.

Customer: They asked for repro steps we can run from our side to simulate Safari behavior. I gave them this list: 
- Repro (origin working): curl -N https://origin.internal/v1/streams?id=abc
- Repro (CDN failing): curl -N https://cdn.example/v1/streams?id=abc --include -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}\n"
- Browser repro: use Safari 16, open devtools network tab, open EventSource to CDN URL, watch for closed connection and compare response headers.
- Quick header check: `curl -I https://cdn.example/v1/streams?id=abc` and verify no gzip, Cache-Control: no-cache, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials present.

Maya Chen: Customer implemented: disabled Cloudflare "Auto Minify" and turned off gzip for SSE path, set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. They report Safari now streams correctly. 

Omar Reyes: Great. Closing loop: create KB note with checklist for SSE + browser issues (CORS credentials, CDN buffering, compression, redirects, headers, Safari quirks). Also add a note to the internal runbook to check for billing spikes on reconnect storms.

Maya Chen: Will file a short KB and attach the curl commands + polyfill snippet. Flagging for product: consider adding a header in Redwood hosted SSE endpoints to opt-out of edge compression and set no-transform by default.

SRE Bot: Log: escalation resolved (customer confirmed). Follow-ups: KB PR created (#4567), product ticket created (RDW-789) to default no-transform on SSE responses.

Benji Patel: Thanks everyone. If we see more customers hit this, we should surface CDN config examples for Cloudflare/CloudFront in our docs. :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: Thanks — closing thread.
